statement: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $|2x - 6| + 4 = 4$?

choices.misconception: I set $2x - 6$ equal to $0$ but moved the $6$ without changing its sign, so I got $2x = -6$ and $x = -3$.
I forgot to subtract $4$ from both sides and solved $|2x - 6| = 4$, using the case $2x - 6 = -4$, which gives $x = 1$.
I forgot to subtract $4$ from both sides and solved $|2x - 6| = 4$, using the case $2x - 6 = 4$, which gives $x = 5$.

hints: Get the absolute value by itself on one side first.
Subtract $4$ from both sides. Which number has an absolute value of $0$?

solutions.reliable: Subtracting $4$ from both sides gives $|2x - 6| = 0$. The only number with absolute value $0$ is $0$, so $2x - 6 = 0$ and $x = 3$. Check: $|0| + 4 = 4$.
